title: The Patience of Moss
statement: For eleven years I have knelt on wet stones with a hand lens. Mosses were the first plants to leave the sea, and they still hold the forest together, a millimetre at a time.

fragments.title: Through the hand lens
fragments.text: At ten times magnification a dull green carpet turns into a cathedral: spiral leaves, glass-like hair points, capsules on red stalks. Nobody believes me until they look.

fragments.title: Drying and waking
fragments.text: Some mosses can dry to a crisp for decades and unfurl within minutes of rain. I time them with a stopwatch. It never stops feeling like resurrection.

fragments.title: The old wall in my street
fragments.text: Forty-one species on a single churchyard wall. I have a map of each one. The council wanted to pressure-wash it; we made a deal.
